evals.expected_output: One report opening with the reviewed commit, the tree state, and the approvability verdict, carrying all eight headings verbatim and in order, and closing with a yes on structural mergeability.
expectations: The report carries all eight headings verbatim and in the documented order: What the changes do and implement; What it retires; What of the existing workflow changes; What is critical; Bugs it may introduce; What should be fixed though it is not a clear bug; Decisions the implementer must make before fixing; Can it be structurally merged as it is.
The report opens with the reviewed commit SHA and the tree state it left behind.
The lead states the verdict on approvability in general together with the shortest path to yes.
The lead names the forge layer as unavailable, because no gh is on PATH for this run.
Each of the seven findings headings carries at least one finding.
Every finding names its location, quotes or reproduces its evidence, states the consequence, proposes a fix, and names who decides.
Every finding outside the critical heading carries a non-blocking label.
Each item under 'Decisions the implementer must make before fixing' is a choice between named options with a suggested default.
The closing answer is yes, and it cites the conflict-free test merge and the ahead and behind counts as its evidence.
The urllib call in src/export.py appears under 'What is critical', citing CHARTER.md by name.
The deleted src/legacy_table.py appears under 'What it retires'.
The changed Makefile test target appears under 'What of the existing workflow changes'.
